compiled_state.description:
## Story DD Coverage
- dd-1: dso_local_id property removed mid-pass → bug filed via .claude/scripts/dso ticket create bug same pass (sc-6)
- dd-2: dso-id-<active-local-id> label without dso_local_id property → does NOT bind via JQL dedup; differ emits exactly one (inbound, repair_property) on first encounter (sc-7)

## Testing Mode
RED

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Unit tests pass (exit 0)
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_check_dual_identity_complete.py
- [ ] Lint passes (exit 0)
  Verify: make lint-ruff
- [ ] Format check passes (exit 0)
  Verify: make format-check
- [ ] check_dual_identity_complete returns (quarantine_keys: set[str], seed_repair_property_mutations: list[Mutation]) tuple covering both failure modes
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_check_dual_identity_complete.py::test_returns_quarantine_and_seed_mutations
- [ ] report_schema_drift filed bug via subprocess CLI with dedup_key bridge-alert:schema-drift:<issue_key>
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_check_dual_identity_complete.py::test_report_schema_drift_dedup_key
- [ ] Per-invariant cap _CAP_PER_PASS=5 honored independently from check_at_most_one's cap (each invariant has its own counter)
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_check_dual_identity_complete.py::test_cap_per_invariant_independent
- [ ] alert_store dedup prevents duplicate bugs on re-invocation
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_check_dual_identity_complete.py::test_dedup_skips_already_filed
- [ ] Existing test_invariants.py + test_at_most_one_invariant.py regressions pass
  Verify: pytest -xvs tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_invariants.py tests/unit/dso_reconciler/test_at_most_one_invariant.py

## Implementation Notes

Mirror the existing check_at_most_one_dso_local_id pattern at invariants.py:63 (subprocess + alert_store + _CAP_PER_PASS dedup + narrow exception handling).

### check_dual_identity_complete signature
```python
def check_dual_identity_complete(
    snapshot: dict,
    repo_root: Path | None = None,
    ticket_cli: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[set[str], list[Mutation]]:
    \"\"\"Returns (quarantine_keys, seed_repair_property_mutations).
    Mode A: property removed → calls report_schema_drift → adds key to quarantine.
    Mode B: orphan label (no matching property AND no other issue binds that local_id) → seeds (inbound, repair_property) mutation.\"\"\"
```

### report_schema_drift narrow seam (Security constraint)
The Story Considerations require a NARROW seam — invariants.py MUST NOT thread the full orchestrator (ticket_cli + alert_store) into the seam itself. Two patterns are acceptable:
- (a) report_schema_drift(issue_key, reason) → returns a structured DriftRecord; caller (check_dual_identity_complete) writes the alert + files the bug via the existing inline pattern.
- (b) Keep report_schema_drift as a private module-internal helper (`_report_schema_drift`) inside invariants.py with full state; the PUBLIC seam exposed to other layers is just `check_dual_identity_complete` (which returns quarantine_keys + seed mutations — no orchestrator-shaped state crosses out).

Implement pattern (b): _report_schema_drift is module-private, fully self-contained. Applier (task-3) does NOT import from invariants — instead, the applier emits a follow-on action signal that reconcile.py routes to a fresh invariant call. (See task-3 amendment for the precise follow-on path.)

### _CAP_PER_PASS semantics
The existing _CAP_PER_PASS = 5 constant (line 10) is shared between invariants. PIN: each invariant has its own per-pass counter — they do NOT share a budget. check_dual_identity_complete tracks violations_filed independently of check_at_most_one_dso_local_id.

### dd-1 closure scope
The throwaway-DIG integration check is the LIVE verification path (post-implementation operator-driven, not in the test suite). Unit-test-with-mocked-ticket-CLI is sufficient for story closure; the throwaway-DIG path is a smoke check during Phase 0 rollout.

## Retry Budget
MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model)
On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages)
On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history
If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately

comments.body: AC amendment (gap G1): Make report_schema_drift PUBLIC (drop the underscore). It is load-bearing for T4's same-pass signal routing. T1 exposes `report_schema_drift(issue_key, reason, *, repo_root, ticket_cli, alert_store)` as a public module-level function. The 'narrow seam' (Security Considerations) is preserved by keeping the function self-contained — callers (reconcile.py) supply only orchestrator-shaped state THEY ALREADY HAVE; the function itself does not import the orchestrator.
comments.author: Test

comments.body: AC amendment (gap G4): Add explicit cross-binding check as a T1 sub-deliverable. check_dual_identity_complete builds an `active_bindings` index at entry: {local_id: jira_key} for every Jira issue whose dso_local_id property is set. For any Mode B candidate (label present, property missing), if the implied local_id appears in active_bindings under a DIFFERENT jira_key, skip seed_repair_property AND quarantine the candidate instead. RED test fixture REQUIRED: local-A bound to DIG-1 via property + DIG-2 has dso-id-localA label without property → expect quarantine on DIG-2 (NOT a repair_property mutation that would create at-most-one conflict).
comments.author: Test

comments.body: AC amendment (gap G5): Disjointness assertion. check_dual_identity_complete MUST assert at return time that quarantine_keys ∩ {m.target for m in seed_repair_property_mutations} == set() — i.e., a key is either quarantined OR seeded, never both. Internal bug → raise InvariantClassificationError immediately rather than letting T4's post-emit filter silently drop a legitimate repair_property.
comments.author: Test

comments.body: AC amendment (gap G6): Document _CAP_PER_PASS semantics. PINNED: _CAP_PER_PASS is PER-INVARIANT, not global. check_at_most_one and check_dual_identity each track violations_filed independently; they do NOT share a budget. Two invariants × cap=5 = up to 10 bugs per pass. Document this in invariants.py module docstring + KNOWN-ISSUES.md (covered in T5).
